title: A new identity for Ninety
question: Which direction should carry the full redesign: Today, Courses, History, Duty Leave, Settings, setup, timetable, and dialogs? All preserve the fixed attendance rules, offline data, native behavior, and the approved neutral-and-blue palette.

options.label: Daily rhythm
options.thesis: A student-radio running order becomes a welcoming, time-led attendance companion.
options.viewport: A compact Ninety masthead; a bold day and progress panel; the primary present action; classes arranged along a continuous time rail.
options.risk: The time rail must stay useful when labs span several periods; no pretend music-player controls.
options.lineage: Campus radio running orders and cue sheets

raised.raise: One clear daily action owns the first viewport.
Numbers have a distinctive, consistent type rhythm.
Course details stay dense and orderly when expanded.
Every visual mark corresponds to real attendance data.

options.label: Campus daybook
options.thesis: A well-loved student planner, expressed as a clean native app with generous breathing room.
options.viewport: A welcoming daily heading; a six-part completion strip; an open list of classes; course summaries read as clearly indexed pages.
options.risk: The most familiar grounded direction: useful and inviting, but closer to established planner apps.
options.lineage: Student weekly planners and university daybooks

options.label: Clear next step
options.thesis: Campus wayfinding directs attention to the next attendance decision.
options.viewport: A strong blue sign band carries the day and one next action; numbered periods and clear arrows organize the remaining route.
options.risk: Exceptionally clear, but potentially more official than personal; airport yellow is translated to the approved blue.
options.lineage: International terminal wayfinding, translated to campus use
options.case: Competitive: strong product clarity; Daily rhythm better matches a personal student routine.

options.label: Semester pass
options.thesis: A journey wallet gives every period a visible, retained record.
options.viewport: A dated daily pass above compact period slips; recorded outcomes remain visible; the day resolves into one completed pass.
options.risk: Clear record ownership, but the ticket metaphor may feel busier than the daily task deserves; carrier colors become the approved neutrals and blue.
options.lineage: Jet-age ticket wallets and sequential coupons
options.case: Competitive: clear retained-record states; Daily rhythm has a stronger connection to student life.

options.label: One period at a time
options.thesis: A full-screen class advances to the next period.
options.viewport: One class fills the screen, with attendance controls beside it.
options.risk: Hides the whole-day overview and makes grouped labs harder to inspect.
options.case: Declined: weaker audience identification and product clarity than Daily rhythm.

options.label: Attendance specimen
options.thesis: A type-led index repeats attendance figures at deliberate scales.
options.viewport: Large period numerals above a tightly indexed class list.
options.risk: Bitmap display adds friction to everyday reading.
options.case: Declined: weaker audience identification and product clarity than Daily rhythm.

options.label: Course catalog
options.thesis: A rigorous catalog gives every course a stable place.
options.viewport: An indexed course list and restrained attendance plots.
options.risk: Coded identification undermines full course names and quick recognition.
options.case: Declined: weaker audience identification and product clarity than Daily rhythm.

options.label: Attendance field
options.thesis: Recorded periods form an exact visual field.
options.viewport: A dense field of period marks sits above the daily action.
options.risk: Abstract density is less welcoming and harder to decode at a glance.
options.case: Declined: weaker audience identification and product clarity than Daily rhythm.
options.kept: Every mark must encode a real fact.

canonCard.label: Familiar Material app
canonCard.thesis: Standard Material 3 navigation and cards, carefully executed.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional toolbar, attendance summary card, stacked class cards, and five navigation destinations.
canonCard.risk: Familiar and dependable; retains much of the stock arrangement you asked to replace.
